takeaway: The transpyloric plane runs through the lower L1, pylorus and first part of the duodenum, the neck of the pancreas, the renal hila and the ninth costal cartilages.

lines.text: The transpyloric plane lies midway between the suprasternal notch and the pubic symphysis.
At the bedside, estimate it halfway between the xiphisternum and the umbilicus.
It runs through the inferior part of L1,
lines.say: It runs through the inferior part of L one,

lines.text: and through the pylorus, the gastroduodenal junction and the first part of the duodenum.
It also crosses the neck of the pancreas,
the hila of the kidneys, and the ninth costal cartilages.
So the answer is the first part of the duodenum.
